description.text: Mauro Piacenza was born in Genoa on 15 September 1944 and entered the priesthood after completing a doctorate summa cum laude in canon law at the Pontifical Lateran University.  He served as a parochial vicar, chaplain to the University of Genoa, and professor of canon law and theology at several institutions before being made a canon of the Genoa Cathedral in 1986.

In 1990 Piacenza joined the staff of the Congregation for the Clergy, rising to Undersecretary in 2000 and Secretary in 2007.  He was appointed Prefect of that Congregation in 2010, created a cardinal deacon by Pope Benedict XVI the same year, and later became Major Penitentiary of the Apostolic Penitentiary in 2013, a position he held until 2024.  He also served as President of the Pontifical Commission for the Cultural Heritage of the Church and as a cardinal elector in the 2013 conclave that elected Pope Francis.

curiosities.text: Piacenza served as Major Penitentiary of the Apostolic Penitentiary from 2013 until his successor was appointed in 2024.
He was one of the cardinal electors who participated in the 2013 papal conclave that elected Pope Francis.
In 2003 he was appointed President of the Pontifical Commission for the Cultural Heritage of the Church, a role that underscored his expertise in canon law and church history.
